source.title: SING: A Plug-and-Play DNN Learning Technique
source.authors: Adrien Courtois; Damien Scieur; J. Morel; P. Arias; Thomas Eboli

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices; no apparent truncation.
record.tranche_reason: Tests optimizer changes and reports held-out performance across image classification, depth estimation, and language tasks. These are new settings for optimizer-related generalization claims; it does not test memorization capacity, width, convolutional bias, or generalization measures from the versions.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper’s own comparisons of SING with host optimizers on validation or test metrics, including reported negative and mixed results. Theoretical claims and cited prior work are not empirical result rows. The RDE results concern a synthetic depth-estimation task, not the natural-label memorization claim.
record.test_reason: Tables 1 and 8 report direct SGD–AdamW comparisons on image classification, bearing on V4 under learning-rate and weight-decay tuning. The extracted SING comparisons alone do not test V4: improving AdamW with a new method does not establish its performance relative to SGD.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly accurate: the authors conclude that SING improves Adam(W) stability and held-out performance across several tasks without additional tunable hyperparameters. Qualify this with unchanged denoising performance, mixed SQuAD metrics, and difficulties with LayerNorm and LayerScale. Their convergence proof does not cover the AdamW combination used in most experiments.
record.recipe_differences: Adds SING gradient centralization and layer-wise normalization to AdamW or other host optimizers; compares task metrics rather than random-label memorization, width sweeps, convolutional bias, or generalization-gap measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and task; optimizer; SING components, including softplus calibration and normalization; model scale on the synthetic depth-estimation task; LayerNorm and LayerScale; learning-rate scheduler and hyperparameter choices.

fits_no_version.finding: SING improves AdamW's reported held-out metrics on several classification and language tasks; SQuAD has mixed exact-match/F1 changes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adding SING can improve AdamW's held-out performance, depending on task and metric.

fits_no_version.finding: On synthetic depth estimation, SING strongly improves several host optimizers, barely improves AdaFactor, and depends on its components.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SING can stabilize optimization and improve synthetic depth-estimation performance, with optimizer- and component-dependent effects.

record.problems: ImageNet experiments were run once per setting; CIFAR100 averages five runs with standard deviations. Fine-tuning reproductions fell below suggested results. Hyperparameter searches were limited for ImageNet and other settings; some optimizer comparisons used defaults. The claimed improvement is task- and architecture-dependent, and schedules differ in some comparisons. No direct measure of the training-test gap is reported.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Component ablations are included where they show convergence failure or outcome changes; additional component ablation comparisons are outside direct V4 optimizer generalization comparisons.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label held-out performance under matched architectures and recipes.
Width sweeps beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
The learning-rate-and-schedule-only tuning regime; matched training performance; adaptive-versus-SGD language comparisons; Adam-to-SGD switching; controlled isolation of decoupled weight decay.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and remedies for large-batch penalties.
Dropout ablations and interactions with training-set size or augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness rankings against measured generalization gaps. Escaping narrow minima does not test this correlation.
Removal of memorized examples versus random removal.

missing.what: Direct ResNet18 CIFAR100 comparison: SGD 75.63%, AdamW 77.95%; AdamW standard deviation 0.15 percentage points across five runs. Record the augmentation, label smoothing, frozen batch-normalization parameters, and learning-rate/weight-decay tuning.
Direct ImageNet ResNet18 comparison: SGD 72.44%, AdamW 72.58%; 88 epochs, batch size 1024, one run per setting. SGD uses the FFCV recipe; AdamW learning rate and weight decay are tuned.
Direct ImageNet ResNet34 comparison: SGD 75.36%, AdamW 75.29%, under the same stated training budget and tuning procedure; one run per setting.

record.verdict_notes: None of R1–R15 directly establishes a listed version; their states are therefore cannot_determine relative to these versions. V4 verdicts instead use omitted SGD–AdamW comparisons in the supplied text. Weight-decay tuning and decoupled AdamW prevent interpreting these results as a clean challenge to the limited-tuning premise.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label fitting or natural-label generalization comparison.
No width sweep beyond interpolation or test-error curve.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
Tests AdamW against AdamW plus SING, rather than the listed SGD comparisons or broad optimizer tuning; does not compare SGD with Adam across these tasks.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or other generalization-measure comparison.

relationships.condition: Broader-tuning qualification: ResNet18 on CIFAR100 and ImageNet-1K
relationships.reason: Text-based verdict pending missing rows: AdamW exceeds SGD, 77.95% versus 75.63% on CIFAR100 and 72.58% versus 72.44% on ImageNet, consistent with adaptive methods winning under recipes that also tune weight decay; ImageNet has one run.
relationships.display_finding: Reported accuracies favor AdamW on CIFAR100 and ImageNet, but these comparisons remain unverified and ImageNet has only one run.

relationships.condition: ResNet34 on ImageNet-1K with the tested tuning recipe
relationships.reason: Text-based verdict pending a missing row: SGD reaches 75.36% and AdamW 75.29%, a 0.07-point difference from single runs, providing little evidence of a substantive adaptive-method penalty.
relationships.display_finding: AdamW reportedly trailed SGD slightly in single runs, but the comparison remains unverified and cannot establish a reliable disadvantage.
